audit_result.proof_trace: The proof fails: `is_obligation_safe` calls `debts_value_usd_non_liquidation` and `collaterals_usd_non_liquidation` sequentially, each fetching per-asset prices via `get_price_with_check`, which reads each coin type's independent `PriceFeedComponent.update_time` (a Pyth off-chain timestamp). No mechanism synchronises these timestamps across assets; `check_price` (user.move:61-69) validates only per-asset staleness (≤5 s each) and makes no cross-asset comparison. The maximum timestamp skew between any collateral price and any debt price in the same health check is therefore up to 5 seconds.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An attacker constructs a Sui PTB that first calls the permissionless `refresh_usd_price<CollateralCoin>` (user.move:14) to stamp the collateral price with the latest Pyth timestamp, then immediately calls `borrow::borrow<MarketType, DebtCoin>` while the debt asset's oracle is at near-maximum staleness (showing a price up to 5 s old); if the debt asset's true price has risen in that window, `is_obligation_safe` underestimates debt value, allowing the attacker to borrow more than their collateral properly supports.

PROP-01b-partial1-inv-027.text: Collateral and debt value calculations must use the same oracle timestamp for consistency.
